verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own OAuth implementation: scoped access for third-party applications, custom OAuth scopes, Client ID Metadata Documents and Dynamic Client Registration, a standards-based device authorization grant, and OIDC as an Enterprise SSO protocol. This shows developers get standard OAuth/OIDC flows without hand-rolling the protocol. The specific flows named in the story are not explicitly documented, and community reports describe refresh-token handling as sparsely documented, though those reports concern Clerk's own session tokens. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the authorization-code-with-PKCE flow, documented refresh-token issuance and rotation for OAuth clients, OIDC discovery and ID-token details, and independent hands-on corroboration.
